reason: Dysostosis, alopecia and ear abnormalities define the syndrome; cleft palate occurs in 3/4. Eyelid coloboma in 1/4 does not warrant ocular involvement.
Vertebral inflammation establishes musculoskeletal disease. Inflammation alone does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another immune-mediated mechanism.
Autonomic neuropathy defines the spectrum; persistent contractures and progressive scoliosis support musculoskeletal involvement. Abnormal sweating alone does not establish skin damage.
Protein S deficiency is a coagulation disorder. Thromboses are separately diagnosed complications, and warfarin-induced skin necrosis is treatment-related.
Subcutaneous tissue and superficial fascia fall within the dermatologic axis; other organs are subtype-dependent.

Neurologic disease defines the concept. Frequent optic nerve abnormalities, skeletal deformities and hearing impairment support the three involved axes; endocrine involvement is acknowledged under the cap.
Parametritis is an infectious form of pelvic inflammatory disease. Its reproductive location has no anatomical axis; other serosal organs are not implicated.
Meningioma originates in meninges, establishing neurologic primary involvement. Skull-base location does not itself establish bone damage or common ocular or endocrine involvement.

Add ocular involvement: progressive myopia is an intrinsic feature in approximately 80% or more of POLR3-related leukodystrophy patients, meeting the common functional impairment rule within the four-axis cap.

corrected.basis: Leukodystrophy, dental abnormalities and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; progressive myopia affects ~80-90%, supporting ocular involvement.
